title: General words for attitude and behavior
blurb: Read the HESI A2 words that describe how people act and feel (diligent, complacent, ambivalent, prudent) and avoid their look-alikes.
question: A preceptor's note calls one student diligent and vigilant, another complacent, and a third ambivalent about night shifts. Which student would you trust with a busy unit, and which words are look-alike traps?

teach.h: Words that label a person's manner
teach.body: Formally, these are adjectives that describe a person's habits, attitude or feelings toward a task or another person. In plain English: they answer 'What is this person like?' Most come in clusters: careful words (diligent, meticulous), risky words (complacent, impulsive), feeling words (ambivalent, indifferent). HESI A2 distractors are usually a look-alike (discreet/discrete) or a trait from the same cluster that is close but different.

head: Word
Meaning
Example
rows: careful to do right and well

teach.caption: The first word's meaning is on the left of each label; the look-alike's is on the right.

teach.body: Marcus Hill, applying to a respiratory therapy program, reads his own reference letters. One calls him 'conscientious and receptive to feedback.' He decodes: conscientious means careful to do the job right; receptive means open to new ideas. A classmate's letter warns she can be 'impulsive but resilient': she acts without thinking but bounces back. Marcus notices that both letters mix strengths and cautions, and each word has one exact meaning.

teach.text: Two classic HESI A2 swaps: averse (unwilling) is not adverse (harmful), and discreet (tactful, private) is not discrete (separate). Also, 'mixed feelings' (ambivalent) is not 'no feelings' (indifferent).

items: Careful: diligent, conscientious, meticulous, vigilant, prudent, proactive.
Strong and open: resilient, tenacious, assertive, receptive, tactful, discreet, benevolent.
Risky or resistant: complacent, impulsive, obstinate, indifferent, ambivalent, skeptical, hesitant, averse, sedentary.
Look-alikes: vigorous, discrete, adverse, tenuous, compliant, ambiguous.
Ambivalent = mixed feelings; indifferent = no interest.

summary: You can now match the HESI A2 attitude words to the habits and feelings they describe, from diligent and prudent to complacent and obstinate. You can also reject the look-alike traps: adverse, discrete, vigorous, tenuous and compliant.

A.q: A conscientious volunteer, Marcus double-checked every visitor badge before letting anyone onto the unit. What is the best definition of the word conscientious in this sentence?
A.why: Conscientious means careful to do what is right and to do work thoroughly.

whyNot.3: Double-checking every badge is the opposite of being bored with the task.

A.q: The proactive nurse scheduled follow-up calls before any patient could miss a medication refill. What is the best definition of the word proactive in this sentence?
A.why: Proactive means acting in advance to deal with an expected problem.

whyNot.0: Reacting after a problem is reactive, the opposite.
whyNot.1: Productive (getting a lot done) is a look-alike; proactive is about timing.
whyNot.3: Provoking conflict is provocative, a look-alike.

A.q: Kim was hesitant to ask questions during her first week of clinical rotations on the unit. What is the best definition of the word hesitant in this sentence?
A.why: Hesitant means slow to act or speak because of doubt; reluctant.

whyNot.0: Eager is the opposite of hesitant.
whyNot.1: Not being allowed is a rule, not a feeling; hesitant describes her own doubt.
whyNot.2: Being busy is a topic fit for a first week, but hesitant is about doubt.

B.q: The workshop taught new nurses to be assertive when reporting unsafe staffing levels to managers. What is the best definition of the word assertive in this sentence?
B.why: Assertive means confident and direct in stating needs or opinions.

whyNot.0: Timid is the opposite of assertive.
whyNot.2: Vague reporting is the opposite of direct.
whyNot.3: Complaining is a topic fit for reporting a problem, but assertive describes confidence, not grumbling.

B.q: Even during the emergency, the charge nurse stayed calm and made rational decisions. What is the best definition of the word rational in this sentence?
B.why: Rational means based on reason or logic.

whyNot.0: Based on emotion is the opposite of rational.
whyNot.1: Limited in amount suggests ration, a look-alike.
whyNot.3: Emergencies are fast, a topic fit, but rational describes logic, not speed.

B.q: After her heart attack, Mrs. Hall was told to avoid vigorous exercise for six weeks. What is the best definition of the word vigorous in this sentence?
B.why: Vigorous means strong, energetic and active; vigorous exercise is intense exercise.

whyNot.3: Gentle exercise is the opposite, and is what she may do.

C.q: Dr. Chen was skeptical of the supplement's claims until she read the clinical trial results. What is the best definition of the word skeptical in this sentence?
C.why: Skeptical means doubting that something is true; she doubted the claims until she saw evidence.

whyNot.1: Hopeful is close to the opposite of doubting.
whyNot.3: She knew about the claims; skeptical means she doubted them, not that she was unaware.

C.q: The patient was receptive to the dietitian's suggestions and started a food diary that same week. What is the best definition of the word receptive in this sentence?
C.why: Receptive means willing to consider new ideas; starting the diary shows she accepted the advice.

whyNot.1: Resistant is the opposite of receptive.
whyNot.3: Puzzlement would not lead her to act at once; receptive means open.

C.q: Select the word that best completes the sentence: When telling the family about the delay, the nurse chose her words carefully and was ____.
C.why: Tactful means sensitive in dealing with others to avoid offense, which is what choosing words carefully shows.

whyNot.0: Tactile means relating to touch, a look-alike.
whyNot.2: Tactical means relating to strategy, another look-alike.
whyNot.3: Tenacious means persistent; nothing in the sentence is about holding firm.

reteach.title: Write the team roster
reteach.question: A coach writes one word next to each player's name on a roster. How would a charge nurse do the same for a shift, and why does each word have to be exact?

blocks.body: A coach might write 'tenacious' next to the defender who never gives up, 'impulsive' next to the striker who shoots too early, and 'complacent' next to the starter who stopped training. A charge nurse could do the same: vigilant for the nurse who spots changes, meticulous for the one who checks every label. Each word is a short, exact profile. Swap in a look-alike and the profile is wrong.

blocks.h: Helpful vs risky on a shift

blocks.text: A vigorous player is energetic; a vigilant one is watchful. Same first letters, different job on the roster.

explain.body: Diligent (hardworking), conscientious (careful to do right), meticulous (attention to detail), vigilant (watchful), prudent (wise about the future), proactive (acts ahead).

test.q: Which word means showing great attention to detail?
test.why: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail.

whyNot.0: Miraculous means like a miracle, a look-alike ending.

explain.body: Complacent (smug, unaware of risk), impulsive (acts without thinking), obstinate (stubborn), indifferent (unconcerned), sedentary (mostly seated).

test.q: The obstinate toddler clamped his mouth shut and turned away from the medicine dropper. What is the best definition of the word obstinate in this sentence?
test.why: Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change or give in.

whyNot.0: A sleepy child would not actively turn away; obstinate means stubborn.
whyNot.3: Fear is a topic fit for a toddler and medicine, but obstinate describes stubborn refusal.

explain.body: Ambivalent means strong but mixed feelings. Indifferent means no real interest. Ambiguous describes a statement, not a feeling: unclear in meaning.

test.q: Which word describes having strong but mixed feelings about a choice?
test.why: Ambivalent means having mixed or contradictory feelings.

whyNot.0: Indifferent means having no particular interest.
whyNot.1: Ambiguous means unclear in meaning, a look-alike.
whyNot.2: Adamant means refusing to change one's mind, the opposite of torn.

explain.body: Averse (to) describes a person who is unwilling or dislikes something. Adverse describes a harmful or unfavorable effect, such as an adverse reaction.

test.q: Many young children are averse to the taste of liquid antibiotics, so pharmacies add flavoring. What is the best definition of the word averse in this sentence?
test.why: Averse means strongly unwilling or disliking; the children dislike the taste.

whyNot.1: Allergy is a topic fit for antibiotics, but averse means disliking, not reacting.
whyNot.3: Accustomed (used to) is close to the opposite of disliking.
